content.title: The Score: Constellation, Chevron, Lockheed Martin and More Stocks That Defined the Week
content.summary: The Modelo and Corona importer reported lower quarterly sales and profit as customers, particularly Hispanic consumers, continue to buy less beer.  Constellation cited weak consumer sentiment and rising unemployment rates, as well as a downturn in “4,000-calorie jobs,” or physically demanding jobs such as construction, that typically boost beer sales.  Constellation shares rose 5.3% Thursday.

content.title: Are ICE Raids Hurting Corona Sales? Constellation Brands Investors Are Wondering Aloud.
content.summary: Are immigration raids hurting Mexican beer sales?  The question might sound both indelicate and frivolous at a time when Americans are hotly divided over the tactics of the Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency, or ICE.  More than half of Constellation’s beer customers are Hispanic.

content.title: STZ Q4 Deep Dive: Margin Pressures and Distribution Gains Shape Outlook
content.summary: Beer, wine, and spirits company Constellation Brands (NYSE:STZ) reported Q4 CY2025 results exceeding the market’s revenue expectations, but sales fell by 9.8% year on year to $2.22 billion. Its non-GAAP profit of $3.06 per share was 16.2% above analysts’ consensus estimates.
